name: linked-zero-work-wavematch-multiple-threadgroup-scatter
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: Zero sort extent selects no scatter work for the one-thread invocation while all direct prefix and postfix callbacks are provided by exact signature-compatible modules. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: wavematch-scatter-float-keys-two-simdgroups-stable-digit-ranks
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-work case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). Constant 124 = 0x80 selects float keys, ascending, no argsort, intermediate source, linked destination. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (two simdgroups, two elements a lane) ranks 100 keys from tempBuffer1 (binding 28) by digit (flipped >> 26) & 255 of their radix-ordered bits (digits [15, 16, 17, 46, 47, 48], all below 64), with tempBuffer5 (binding 24) holding each digit's starting offset (the exclusive prefix of the digit counts; zero for digits 192 and up, which the lane-sum step reads). The ranking counts digits per simdgroup in the threadgroup's packed 16-bit counters (two simdgroups share each 32-bit atomic word), takes the exclusive prefix across the simdgroups, ranks lanes within a step by ballot masks, and writes each key through the linked float destination callback at its rank, so the 100 words are the keys stably counting-sorted by digit (many ties, so stability is observed) and the last two keep their fill. Each position is written once; counts are integers exact in any atomic order. Every loop is finite: 16 element steps, 8 ballot rounds, 256 / 64 bin steps.

name: three-lane-statistics-fold-over-one-simd-group
rationale: One 32-thread threadgroup is exactly one SIMD group, so reductionGroups = 32 gives each lane a single pass over nine strided source columns and the shader reaches air.simd_sum.v3f32, air.simd_min.v3f32 and air.simd_max.v3f32 twice: once across the 32 lanes, and once more after lane 0 stages the result in threadgroup memory and the second fold reads it back against the +/-FLT_MAX identities. Every source value is a small integer in [-50,50], so each 32-lane sum stays under 1600 and is exact in f32 whatever order the reduction associates in -- the case cannot be sensitive to lane order. rcpPixels is 2^-5, so the mean is a pure exponent shift and also exact. The three written texels are mean (-0.4375, -0.03125, 0.375), min (-50, -48, -49) and max (47, 50, 49), each channel drawn from a different source column so a transposed or collapsed fold cannot reproduce them.

name: five-overlapping-integer-read-modify-writes
rationale: Overlapping-fragment ordering of an integer framebuffer fetch (DESIGN D198): five instances of the fullscreen triangle each store count * 3 + (1, 2, 3, 4) over the rgba32_uint value they read, wrapping, so lane k of each pixel ends at c * 243 + (k + 1) * 121 mod 2^32 only when every fragment read its predecessor's write. Authored lanes include 0, 0xFFFFFFFF - p, 0x80000000-based, and multiplicative-hash values so the wrap is exercised.

name: per-sample-integer-read-modify-writes-at-4x
rationale: Integer framebuffer fetch in a 4-sample pass (DESIGN D310): three overlapping instances each store count * 3 + (1, 2, 3, 4), wrapping, so n ordered fragments leave c * 3^n + (k + 1) * (3^n - 1) / 2 in lane k of every sample. Every sample of the 2x2 rgba32_uint target starts distinct (pixel p, sample s: 7p + s, 1000 + 16p + s, 0xFFFFFFF0 + s, 3p) and every sample is compared, never resolved.

name: signed-extraction-and-sixty-four-bit-counts
rationale:
Eight uncovered air.* families in one invocation: air.insert_bits.{u.i32,s.i32,u.i64}, air.extract_bits.{s.i32,u.i64}, air.popcount.v2i64 and air.clz.i64 / air.ctz.i64. All thirteen words were derived by hand before the GPU was asked and all thirteen came back as derived.

extract_bits(0xABCDEF01, 8, 8) as a SIGNED extract is -17, not 239. The extracted field is 0xEF, whose top bit is set, and the signed member of the family sign-extends it out of the field width while the unsigned one zero-extends. That distinction is the AIR name's `.s.` versus `.u.` and nothing else, so a lowering that reads the name wrongly answers 239 here.

The 64-bit lanes are the second point. clz(1<<32) is 31 and ctz(1<<32) is 32: the set bit is exactly at the 32-bit boundary, so a lowering that counted in 32 bits and widened, or that truncated the operand, cannot produce both. clz(0) and ctz(0) are both 64 -- Metal's contract is the WIDTH, while GLSL.std.450's FindUMsb and FindILsb answer -1 for a zero operand, so a lowering that reached for those directly answers 0xFFFFFFFF twice. The 64-bit insert writes eight bits starting at offset 30, which straddles the word boundary: the result is 0xFFFFFFC03FFFFFFF, and both halves are read back so a lowering that only cleared within one word is visible.

popcount of a ulong2 counts 64 in the all-ones lane and 32 in 0x0123456789ABCDEF, which is the vector-of-64-bit shape that has no scalar equivalent in the corpus.

The two 32-bit inserts share their operands so the pair differs only in the declared signedness of base and insert -- the answer must be the same bit pattern either way, 0xFFFF5AFF and 0xABCD5A01, which holds the ordinary path beside the sign-sensitive extract above.

The fourteenth word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: quad-and-simdgroup-fills-by-a-function-constant-modulo-of-3
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads, two full simdgroups. Metal answers a fill's modulo by whether it is a constant (D595 item 7): a constant m fills the simdgroup in segments of the next power of two of m, at least 2 (past 32, of the power whose exponent is that one's modulo 8), in either scope; a runtime modulo moves the lanes only when it is a power of two from 2 to the group's width (2 and 4 for a quad, up to 32 for a simdgroup), and otherwise leaves each lane its own data. Thread or vertex t reads in[t] (1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 or -0.5) and fills with in[t] + 1000. The modulo is the function constant 3, which the AIR loads at run time and Metal specializes when it makes the pipeline; thread t writes the quad fill up by 1 and the simdgroup fill down by 2 by it. The translation takes it as a runtime modulo, so this case pins Metal's answer, a known difference while it differs (D595 item 7).

name: quad-and-simdgroup-fills-by-constant-moduli-in-a-fragment-function
rationale: Drawn over an 8x8 target. Metal answers a fill's modulo by whether it is a constant (D595 item 7): a constant m fills the simdgroup in segments of the next power of two of m, at least 2 (past 32, of the power whose exponent is that one's modulo 8), in either scope; a runtime modulo moves the lanes only when it is a power of two from 2 to the group's width (2 and 4 for a quad, up to 32 for a simdgroup), and otherwise leaves each lane its own data. Pixel (x, y) holds x + 64y and fills with 10000 more; it returns the quad fill up by 1 modulo 3 (in fours), down by 1 modulo 5 (in eights, past the quad, over the pixels Metal packs into its simdgroup), and the simdgroup fills up by 2 modulo 3 and down by 1 modulo 33.

name: quad-fills-rotation-first-lane-and-prefixes-in-a-vertex-function
rationale: Sixty-four rasterization-disabled points, two full simdgroups on Apple GPUs. Thread or vertex t reads in[t] (1, -1, 2, -2, 0.5 or -0.5) and fills with in[t] + 1000. Vertex v writes the quad fill up by 1, the fill down by 1 modulo 2, quad_shuffle_rotate_up by 1, quad_broadcast_first, the exclusive prefix sum and the inclusive prefix product of in[v]: quad operations with no quad reduction, which lower to the shuffle and ballot classes.

name: gradient-form-public-prefix-sources-four-channels-flipped-3x2-kernel
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero dimensions stop the kernel before its loads and whose retained prefix callbacks return constants. This case runs the data-gradient form (constant 124 = 0x5834e8: kIsGradient, kIsUnitStride, data format 1, weights format 0, log2 tiles N 0, K 5, X 3, Y 2, C 3), which reads the incoming gradient through prefixTertiary_f and the weights through prefixSecondary_f, both from the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_prefix_secondary_tertiary_f_from_buffers (owned MSL, DESIGN D431 item 2): element c.x + 4 (c.y + 4 (c.z + 4 c.w)) of table array 2 and 1. prefixPrimary_f keeps its retained module (the gradient form does not call it); the writer is the retained postfixPrimary_f (module aad641ec), which stores at word coordinate.x of array 1. Constant 122 = 0x10101 gives the table three arrays. Parameters (binding 29): 3 incoming-gradient channels, 4 output channels, a 3 x 2 kernel, one group and batch, a 2 x 2 incoming gradient, a 1 x 1 destination, offsets (-1, 0), 6 kernel taps (one 8-channel block times six positions), magic divisors 6 (kW kH) and 3 (kW), the others 1. One threadgroup of 128 threads (2304 bytes of threadgroup memory): each iteration loads gradient and flipped-kernel weight values behind channel and image bounds, synchronizes, accumulates 8 steps, and synchronizes again. Data format 1 permutes the data coordinate (x, y, c, n) to (c, x, y, n), so gradient value (c, x, y) is array 2 element c + 4x + 16y, and the destination coordinate (x, y, k, n) to (k, x, y, n), so output channel k lands on word k; the weight coordinate (kW-1-kx, kH-1-ky, k, c) becomes (c, k, kW-1-kx, kH-1-ky), array 1 element c + 4 (k + 4 ((2 - kx) + 4 (1 - ky))). The tap at x = -1 is skipped. Gradient ((5c + 3x + 7y) mod 9) - 4, or 4.5 where that is zero; weights ((7i + 3) mod 11) - 5, or 0.5 where that is zero, 112 of them. Array 1 serves as weights and destination: every weight load precedes the loop's last barrier and every write follows it, and there is one threadgroup, so the result does not depend on scheduling. Expected words 0 to 7 of array 1: outputs [50.0, -21.0, 32.5, -17.0] and the untouched weights [4.0, 0.5, -4.0, 3.0]. Every product is a multiple of 1/4 of magnitude at most 22.5 and every sum is below 2^9, so every word is exact in any summation order; no output is zero. Every loop is bounded: 6 iterations of the tap loop and a fixed 8 inner steps.

name: linked-zero-work-ndarray-convolution2d
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: Zero convolution dimensions select no output work for the sole invocation and preserve the poisoned destination; all direct callbacks use exact signature-compatible modules. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: cube-four-gelu-lanes-past-the-tanh-saturation
rationale: One invocation with gid (0, 0, 0). The activation_params bounds W, H, C4 and n_batch are all 1, so all three guards pass and the kernel reads texel (0, 0) of array slice 0, applies GELU to the four float lanes, and writes them back to slice 0 of the destination. The four lanes are chosen so air.fast_pow.v4f32, air.fast_sqrt.f32 and air.fast_tanh.v4f32 are all byte-exact despite being approximations: tanh reaches exactly 1.0f in binary32 past about 9.011, so any inner polynomial well beyond that has one representable answer no matter how the three functions are approximated, and on the saturated side GELU is the identity because 0.5 * x * (1 + 1) is x with no rounding. Lane 0 takes 30, whose polynomial reaches about 987 and is cut back by air.fast_clamp.v4f32 to the 30 the shader allows. Lanes 1 and 3 take 8 and 6, whose polynomials reach about 24.65 and 12.49 and pass the clamp untouched, so the lanes cover both sides of it. Lane 2 takes -8 and saturates the other way, making 1 + tanh exactly zero and the product a negative zero, which both backends produce despite no-signed-zeros-fp-math on the entry. The results are (30, 8, -0, 6): the cube in air.fast_pow.v4f32 is what carries lane 3's polynomial from 4.79 to 12.49 and lane 1's from 6.38 to 24.65, so a pow that returned the base, its square, or a constant drops those lanes below the saturation threshold and moves the bytes.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel, which is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: dual-half4-zero-target-0
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns zero for both half4 color outputs; this case selects attachment 0 so each distinct eight-byte write is qualified independently while both poisoned attachments are bound in the same render pass.

name: dual-half4-zero-target-1
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns zero for both half4 color outputs; this case selects attachment 1 so each distinct eight-byte write is qualified independently while both poisoned attachments are bound in the same render pass.

name: half-sin-cos-tan-and-sincos-of-the-infinities-without-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads the half pattern in[i] as x, one of +0, -0, +inf and -inf (0x0000, 0x8000, 0x7c00, 0xfc00), and writes one uint4: sin(x) | cos(x) << 16, tan(x) | s << 16, c, and the pattern of x, where s = sincos(x, c). The zeros anchor the finite answers: cos of a zero is 1, and sin, tan and sincos's sine of a zero are a zero, whose sign the case records. Compiled without fast math: no call carries a fast-math flag, so an infinite operand asks a defined question whose answer is a NaN. Question (WP-MLO, TODO 2.8, DESIGN D324 item 2): which NaN Metal answers for each function of each infinity; WP-UNV's probes (UNV-metal-probe-1, WRG-math-probe) read 0x7e00 for every one on the M3 Max and the M4, and the product answers 0x7e00 where the float routine answers a half call. The case holds that answer on every venue.

name: hlg-tone-map-reads-a-ushort-texel-past-the-signed-range
rationale: On a 1x1 grid every value this Dolby-Vision tone mapper computes is fixed by what the manifest binds. inTextureY is rgba16_uint, so air.read_texture_2d.u.v4i16 returns all four stored components and air.convert.f.v4f32.u.v4i16 is the only thing that turns them into floats. Two lanes sit above 32767 on purpose: lane 2 is 40000 and lane 3 is 49152, so a signed convert would read -25536 and -16384 and change both halves of the output. Lane 3 is read back directly -- it is scaled by the binary32 nearest of one third, and 49152 times that rounds to exactly 16384, which binary16 holds exactly, so alpha carries the convert with no rounding of its own. Lanes 0 to 2 reach the output through the shuffle to (lane2, lane1, lane0) and the 1/1023 scale that drives three air.sample_texture_1d.v4f32 coordinates. hlg2LTable has two texels and the module's constexpr sampler is clamp_to_edge, linear, normalized (AIR word 0x7bff0000080a49), so a coordinate at or below zero returns texel 0 exactly and one at or above 0.75 returns texel 1 exactly; lanes (0, 0, 40000) therefore sample (1, 0, 0), which a dropped or reversed shuffle would turn into (0, 0, 1) and a signed convert into (0, 0, 0). preRGBtoRGB_matrix has only an x column, so that triple picks out (1, 2, 4), and RGBtoY_coefs of (1/64, 1/64, 0) make the luma 3/64. That is below the 1/12 branch threshold, so the phi takes the air.fast_sqrt.f32 arm and never reaches air.fast_log.f32, whose MoltenVK variant would not agree; 3 times 3/64 is 9/64 and its root is 3/8 exactly. 3/8 lands a quarter of the way between the two scalingFactorTable texels, so the linear blend of 4 and 8 is exactly 5 and the branch is observable rather than folded away. apply_macos_gamma is false, so the tail is a multiply by Saturation rather than air.fast_pow.v3f32, and every intermediate -- (5, 10, 20), (0.625, 2.5, 1.25) and the final (1.25, 5, 2.5) -- is a dyadic rational binary16 holds exactly, so the fptrunc is lossless and no association order changes a dot.

name: half-math-functions-at-the-lanes-devices-answer-otherwise-without-fast-math
rationale: Each of 32 threads writes 8 words, two halves each, for its half pair (a, b), compiled without fast math (-fno-fast-math): (sin a, cos a), (tan a, asin a), (acos a, atan a), (atan2(a, b), fmod(a, b)), (sqrt a, rsqrt a), (pow(a, b), powr(a, b)), (sinpi a, cospi a), and (tanpi a, b). Operands, 32 (a, b) half pairs: both zeros (the signs of sin, tan, asin, and atan of a zero); fmod(x, +-inf) at x = +0, -0, 1, -1, 2.5, -2.5 (Metal answers x); fmod(1.5, -0.75) (an exact zero); sqrt(65504) (255.875 correctly rounded); atan2, pow, and powr at (3, 7), (-0.300048828125, 0.7001953125), and (7, 3); then 0.5, -0.5, 0.25, 100, -100, 0.999, 2, the smallest normal and 2^-13, the smallest denormals of both signs, 1000, +-3.14, 0.75, 60000, +-6.5, and 1 against various b, and fmod(1, 0). Question (WP-TRN, DESIGN D297): Metal's half answers at the lanes where a device, or the translation's float routines rounded to half, were seen to differ, so the venues' answers can be read against Metal's afresh.

name: clear-first-vfx-curve-info-word-2
rationale: Two loop-free invocations exercise both sides of the thread_position_in_grid.x equality branch: index zero atomically clears the first word of the 20-byte curve record, while index one leaves every remaining poisoned byte untouched.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: scatter-sixteen-argmax-gradients-into-four-contended-atomic-float-slots
rationale:
No authored case reached the multi-block arm of the emitted-graph inliner. This kernel's atomic_float_sum helper is a `fastcc` callee with three blocks and a CAS retry loop, and it is called from inside the caller's own nested loop, so inlining it has to split a loop-body block that already carries OpLoopMerge and OpSelectionMerge and re-derive both. That drives six functions in passes/emitted_inline/mod.rs that nothing cased reaches -- construct_label_ids, block_index_by_label, redirect_terminator_target, rewrite_structured_merge, lift_loop_merge_from_split_tail's helper as_id_ref, and split_inlined_selection_merge -- plus air.atomic.global.cmpxchg.weak.i32 with its expected-value operand in an alloca, air.atomic.global.load.i32, and air.convert.s.i32.f.f32.

The dispatch is 4x4x1 threads in 2x2x1 threadgroups, so there are four threadgroups of four threads and threads_per_threadgroup is (2, 2). Each thread runs a grid-stride pair of loops, y over {lid.y, lid.y+2} and x over {lid.x, lid.x+2}, so a threadgroup covers a 4x4 tile in sixteen iterations. result_strides (params member 12) gives the source and index tile base as 32*gy + 16*gx with row stride 4, which tiles the sixty-four-element source and index buffers exactly; source_strides (member 10) gives the destination base as 8*gy + 4*gx. The two stride members are used crosswise by the kernel, which is what makes swapping them visible: the four bases would become 0, 16, 32, 48 into a sixteen-slot region.

Every one of the sixteen iterations of a threadgroup is an atomic add, and they land on only four slots, so all four threads contend on every slot. The index buffer holds the local slot as a float -- 2*(y/2) + x/2 -- so the four contributions to a slot come from the four DISTINCT lane parities (y%2, x%2), and the source element at that lane carries weight 1, 2, 4 or 8 by parity times m = 1 + 4*slot, where slot is the absolute destination index 8*gy + 4*gx + local. A lost update, a duplicated one, or a contribution that lands in the wrong slot therefore changes the sum by an amount that names which lane and which slot it came from.

The comparison is exact and the adds are `fadd fast`, so the case is association-proof by construction: the four weights sum to 15, every partial sum is an integer below 2^24, and float32 holds all of them exactly whatever order the CAS loop resolves the four threads in. Slot i starts at 1000 + i and must end at 1015 + 61*i. The destination buffer is sixty-four floats, four times the sixteen slots the kernel may touch, and slots 16..63 hold 9000 + i and must survive: a mis-derived base or stride writes into them and names the slot it hit instead of running off the allocation.

execution_safety is authored_bounded. The AIR has three CFG cycles. The outer y loop and the inner x loop are bounded by result_dims.h and result_dims.w (members 11.2 and 11.3, bytes 88 and 92, both authored 4) against a stride of threads_per_threadgroup, so each runs exactly two iterations per thread. The third is the helper's CAS retry loop, which has no authored bound and needs none: air.atomic.global.cmpxchg.weak.i32 is a real atomic, so at each round at least one of the four contending threads commits and leaves the loop, and the loop is bounded above by the number of threads still contending.

name: scatter-six-tracking-records-through-a-half-away-from-zero-round
rationale:
air.fast_round.v2f32 and air.convert.u.i32.f.f16 had no authored case; 49 corpus sources sit behind them. The host is an optical-flow forward warp: each thread reads a flow vector, rounds its own coordinate plus that vector to a destination texel, packs a confidence and its own coordinate into one word, and scatters it with two unsigned atomic maxima.

The flow texture is sampled through the module's linear pixel sampler at integer pixel coordinates, so every fraction is a half and four taps contribute; the texture is constant, so the four equal taps sum back to the value exactly and nothing rests on filter precision. The flow it holds is (0.5, 1.5), which puts BOTH rounds on a tie - the destination is only right if air.fast_round breaks ties away from zero the way Metal does rather than the way GLSL.std.450 Round leaves to the implementation. The confidence texture is sampled through the module's other sampler, which is nearest, so each thread reads its own texel and the six writing threads get six different confidences: one that truncates on a half (1022.5 -> 1022), one that saturates above the clamp ceiling, one that saturates below zero, one exactly on the ceiling, and two exact integers.

The rounds carry three threads of each axis out of the 4x4 bounds, so 26 of the 32 words must keep their initial value untouched - that is the bounds test. The six that write land on six distinct slots, so there is no contention and the answer is deterministic. Every slot starts at 0x40000000, chosen so the maximum genuinely decides: five of the twelve writes lose to the initial value and are dropped. Two of the winning writes are above 0x80000000, so a signed maximum would drop them where the unsigned one the AIR asks for keeps them. All 128 bytes were derived by hand; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.

name: tone-map-through-three-one-dimensional-tables
rationale:
Covers air.sample_texture_1d.u.v4i16, the highest-count uncovered symbol with an authorable host (52 case-less sources), and with it the whole 1D sampling family this shader leans on: three air.sample_texture_1d.v4f32 through a normalized linear sampler, three air.sample_texture_1d.u.v4i16 through a pixel-coordinate nearest one, plus air.read_texture_2d.u.v4i16, air.sample_texture_2d.u.v4i16 and air.dot.v3f16.

One thread at gid (0,0). The kernel indexes a 2054-texel ushort polynomial table three times: at the luma sample shifted right by six, and at the two chroma samples shifted right by six and OR'd with 1024 and 2048. The inputs 192, 128 and 320 make those indices 3, 1026 and 2053, and the table holds 4096, 2048 and 2048 there and zero at all 2051 other texels -- so any texel the lowering reaches other than the three intended ones is a zero and moves the answer. The pixel-coordinate sampler is what makes those indices texel indices at all.

The three lookups feed (luma, chroma0, chroma1) into (v - (0, 2048, 2048)) * 2^-12, giving exactly (1, 0, 0): 4096 and 2048 are powers of two, so both the half conversion and the scale are exact. Zero chroma is what collapses the rest -- the squared chroma term is zero, so the saturation factor is exactly one whatever s2t_ratio holds, and the two chroma lanes stay zero through every later multiply. Saturation is set to zero and trim_sat to one so the remaining scale is the identity.

Both float tables are read past their last texel under clamp-to-edge, which is the one place a linear sampler is exact regardless of the filter weight: the luma coordinate 1.0 on a four-texel table lands at 3.5 and the tone-map coordinate 2.0 at 7.5, and both clamp to texel 3, where the tables hold 2.0 and 1.0. That makes the vector into the final matrix exactly (1, 1, 1), and the half3x3 rows (1,0,0), (0,2,0) and (1,1,1) turn it into (1, 2, 3) under any association or fused multiply-add. Expected output texel is (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0) -- the alpha lane is the shader's own constant one.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-64-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (offset 0, 256 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[n][k] (row stride w_ld = 48 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in half and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the half inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-half
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A one-thread zero-extent half quantized matrix multiply bounds reachable loops and retains the poisoned destination; both direct callbacks use exact signature-compatible modules. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: blit-through-the-decoder-of-a-full-quality-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_blit in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen; buffer 0 is the same map as a rasterization_rate_map literal (DESIGN D235.10), and texture 0 an r32_uint screen image whose texel (x, y) holds 1000y + x + 7. Each fragment maps its [[position]] to screen coordinates through the decoder and writes the screen texel there into an r32_uint target that holds 0xffffffff before the draw (load action). The map is of full quality (one sample of 1.0 per axis), which Metal compiles as the identity (on Apple M3 a quality-1 map's physical size is its screen size, D265's probe), so every pixel is one fragment at its center. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region (DESIGN D269.6): the identity is one region, the whole screen, so the observation is exact.

name: blit-through-the-decoder-of-a-graded-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_blit in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen; buffer 0 is the same map as a rasterization_rate_map literal (DESIGN D235.10), and texture 0 an r32_uint screen image whose texel (x, y) holds 1000y + x + 7. Each fragment maps its [[position]] to screen coordinates through the decoder and writes the screen texel there into an r32_uint target that holds 0xffffffff before the draw (load action); the output is the map's physical region. The map is graded: across, quality 1 at both edges and 0.25 in the middle; down, 0.25 at the top and 1 at the bottom, on a 120x60 screen. Apple M3 compiles it (DESIGN D269.1) to tiles of 32:32, 53:32, 32:32 and 3:3 across and 41:32 and 19:19 down, a 99x51 physical image. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region (DESIGN D269.6): three bands across (the two one-to-one runs apart) by two down, six regions. The decoder's answers carry PrecisionNote::RasterizationRateMap (DESIGN D269.4), so a texel whose decoded point lies within the measured bound of a whole pixel may differ from Metal's.

name: blit-through-the-decoder-of-a-skewed-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_blit in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen; buffer 0 is the same map as a rasterization_rate_map literal (DESIGN D235.10), and texture 0 an r32_uint screen image whose texel (x, y) holds 1000y + x + 7. Each fragment maps its [[position]] to screen coordinates through the decoder and writes the screen texel there into an r32_uint target that holds 0xffffffff before the draw (load action). The map is D235.8's skewed 37x23 map (horizontal 0.5 then 1.0, vertical 1.0 then 0.5), which Apple M3 compiles to a 36x23 physical image (D235.8, D265's probe); the output is that physical region, the texels Metal's pass rasterizes. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region into the same 36x23 physical image (DESIGN D269.6): two regions, 33 screen pixels to 32 then 4 to 4, by one row band. The decoder's answers carry PrecisionNote::RasterizationRateMap (DESIGN D269.4), so a texel whose decoded point lies within the measured bound of a whole pixel may differ from Metal's.

name: a-cache-entry-round-tripped-through-a-stack-copy
rationale: vfx_irradiance_cache_indirect_update copies 296 bytes of a 304-byte cache entry out of the device buffer into a stack allocation and, a few instructions later, copies the same bytes back: llvm.memcpy.p0.p1.i64 followed by llvm.memcpy.p1.p0.i64, the two address-space pairings no case reached before. The round trip is a no-op only if BOTH copies are faithful, so any dropped, truncated or misaligned byte shows up as a difference in bytes 8..303 of entry 0, while the two fields the kernel really updates (offset 0 rewritten unchanged, offset 4 incremented from 3 to 4) pin that it ran at all. A second untouched entry follows, so an over-copy past the 304-byte stride is visible too. The grid is a single thread because the kernel's other output is placed at a slot handed out by an atomic add, whose order across threads is not fixed.

name: a-float-imageblock-member-read-into-a-ushort-beside-it
rationale: DESIGN D281: imageblock_transition reads b (a half at byte 2) and sum (a float at byte 8) of its master through one view and writes a = b + 1, tag = (x, y, 7, 9), and n = ushort(sum * 2) through another. The float plane holds values whose doubles are exact and below 65536 (0 to 32767, halves and quarters), so n is the truncated double: 0, 1, 3, 4, 15, 200, 2000, 4095, 8191, 32766, 65534, 0, 6, 21, 511, 24691. Observes the ushort n plane, so a float member authored in its own R32Float format, at its master offset, reaches the function exactly.
